question:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the question based on the passage:

Sleep occupies roughly a third of the human lifespan, yet its purpose is frequently dismissed as mere idleness. Far from being a passive state, sleep orchestrates a cascade of restorative processes, from consolidating memories to clearing the metabolic waste that accumulates in the brain during waking hours. Chronic sleep deprivation, even when only partial, has been shown to erode concentration, weaken immune defences, and heighten susceptibility to mood disorders. Paradoxically, excessive sleep is not a straightforward remedy; prolonged slumber has been correlated, though not conclusively, with certain metabolic irregularities.

The quantity of rest a person needs is far from uniform, hinging on age, genetic predisposition, and daily exertion. Although popular guidance prescribes a rigid eight hours, contemporary researchers champion a more flexible standard, urging individuals to heed signals such as daytime alertness and the ease with which they fall asleep. Moreover, the quality of sleep, not merely its duration, proves decisive; fragmented rest disturbed by artificial light or late stimulants can be far more damaging than a shorter but uninterrupted night.

In an era saturated with glowing screens and relentless schedules, safeguarding sleep demands deliberate discipline rather than passive hope.

 

Which of the following best captures the author's central argument about sleep in modern life?
option_1: People sleep too little only because official guidelines are too rigid.
option_2: Securing adequate, good-quality sleep demands conscious discipline in a screen-dominated age.
option_3: People wrongly assume that sleeping for longer is always healthier.
option_4: A person's sleep requirement is dictated almost entirely by genetics.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Securing adequate, good-quality sleep demands conscious discipline in a screen-dominated age.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The closing line — "safeguarding sleep demands deliberate discipline" — together with the reference to glowing screens and relentless schedules identifies the author's core concern: modern life makes healthy sleep hard, so it must be pursued deliberately. (सचेत अनुशासन)

 

• The passage stresses both quantity and quality of sleep; the option that best 'captures' the argument must reflect this effortful protection of sleep rather than a single narrow cause.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (rigid guidelines): The author does criticise the rigid eight-hour rule, but this is a supporting detail, not the central argument.

 

• Option 3 (longer is not healthier): Over-sleeping is mentioned only tentatively ('though not conclusively'); it is not the main thrust.

 

• Option 4 (genetics alone): Genetics is listed as merely one of several factors, so 'almost entirely' is an overstatement.

 

NOTE

 

• In main-idea questions, pick the option that spans the whole passage; extreme words such as 'only', 'always' and 'entirely' usually mark a distractor.

Read the following passage carefully and answer the question based on the passage:

The quantity of rest a person needs is far from uniform, hinging on age, genetic predisposition, and daily exertion. Although popular guidance prescribes a rigid eight hours, contemporary researchers champion a more flexible standard, urging individuals to heed signals such as daytime alertness and the ease with which they fall asleep. Moreover, the quality of sleep, not merely its duration, proves decisive; fragmented rest disturbed by artificial light or late stimulants can be far more damaging than a shorter but uninterrupted night.

In an era saturated with glowing screens and relentless schedules, safeguarding sleep demands deliberate discipline rather than passive hope.

 

In the context of the passage, the word "erode" most nearly means:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. gradually diminish.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the passage, sleep deprivation is said to erode concentration — i.e. to wear it away slowly and progressively, not all at once. Erode literally means to wear away gradually. (धीरे-धीरे क्षय करना)

 

• The parallel verbs 'weaken' and 'heighten susceptibility' confirm a slow, damaging effect, matching 'gradually diminish'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (abruptly halt): 'Abruptly' contradicts the gradual sense of erosion.

 

• Option 2 (strengthen): The opposite of the intended meaning.

 

• Option 3 (conceal): To hide something is unrelated to wearing it away.

 

NOTE

 

• Vocabulary-in-context questions test the meaning as used, not a dictionary favourite — always plug the option back into the sentence to verify.

question:
Select the word that is the most suitable substitute for the underlined word in the sentence.

The conservator restored each fragile fresco meticulously, overlooking not a single hairline crack.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. scrupulously.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Meticulously means showing great attention to detail; being very careful and precise. (अत्यंत सावधानीपूर्वक)

 

• Scrupulously means with painstaking exactness and care — a near-exact synonym, reinforced by 'overlooking not a single hairline crack'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (carelessly): A direct antonym.

 

• Option 3 (hastily): Doing something hurriedly contradicts careful precision.

 

• Option 4 (reluctantly): Refers to unwillingness, not care.

 

NOTE

 

• Related words: fastidious, punctilious, assiduous all convey painstaking care and are frequent CGL synonym options.

question: Identify the sentence that contains a relative clause.
option_1: Overwhelmed by fatigue, the marathoner collapsed at the finish line.
option_2: As soon as the bell rang, the pupils filed out quietly.
option_3: The economist who predicted the collapse was widely vindicated.
option_4: The tide receded, exposing the barnacled rocks.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The economist who predicted the collapse was widely vindicated.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A relative clause begins with a relative pronoun (who, which, that, whose, whom) and modifies a noun. Here 'who predicted the collapse' describes the noun 'economist'. (सम्बंधवाचक उपवाक्य)

 

• It answers 'which economist?', functioning as an adjective — the defining test of a relative (adjective) clause.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: 'Overwhelmed by fatigue' is a participial phrase, not a clause (no subject + finite verb).

 

• Option 2: 'As soon as the bell rang' is an adverbial clause of time.

 

• Option 4: 'exposing the barnacled rocks' is a participial phrase, not a relative clause.

 

NOTE

 

• Distinguish a relative clause (who/which/that + describes a noun) from an adverbial clause (when/because/if + modifies the verb) and a participial phrase (verb+ing/verb+ed, no finite verb).

question:
Read the sentence and identify the type of the underlined clause.

What the auditor discovered alarmed the entire board of directors.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Noun clause.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The underlined clause 'What the auditor discovered' works as the subject of the verb 'alarmed' — it names a thing, exactly as a noun would. (संज्ञा उपवाक्य)

 

• A clause that occupies a noun position (subject/object/complement) and often begins with what, that, whether, why, how is a noun clause.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Adverbial): Would modify the verb and begin with when/because/if — not the case here.

 

• Option 2 (Relative): Would describe a preceding noun; there is no noun before it to modify.

 

• Option 3 (Conditional): Requires an 'if/unless' condition, which is absent.

 

NOTE

 

• Quick test: if you can replace the clause with 'it' or 'something' ('Something alarmed the board'), it is a noun clause.

question:
Fill in the blank with the correctly spelt word.

His prolonged absence from the crucial meetings was ________ to everyone present.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. conspicuous.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct spelling is conspicuous (con-spic-u-ous), meaning clearly visible or attracting notice. (स्पष्ट/ध्यानाकर्षक)

 

• The root is Latin conspicere ('to look at'); note the sequence -cu-ous, not '-cous' or '-quous'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (conspicous): Omits the 'u' — misspelt.

 

• Option 3 (conspiquous): Wrongly inserts 'qu' — misspelt.

 

• Option 4 (conspicuious): Adds an extra 'i' — misspelt.

 

NOTE

 

• Same family: conspicuously, inconspicuous. Watch the -uous ending shared by 'ambiguous', 'contiguous', 'ingenuous'.

question:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

The new recruits found it hard to adjust to the workload and could not cope up with the relentless deadlines.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. cope up with.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct expression is 'cope with', not 'cope up with'. The word 'up' is redundant — 'cope up with' is a common Indian-English error. (सहना/निपटना)

 

• Correct sentence: '...could not cope with the relentless deadlines.'
◦ Example: She learned to cope with stress, not 'cope up with' stress.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (found it hard): Correct idiomatic structure ('find it hard to').

 

• Option 2 (adjust to): Correct — 'adjust to' takes the preposition 'to'.

 

• Option 4 (deadlines): Correct noun with no error.

 

NOTE

 

• Similar redundancy traps: 'discuss about', 'return back', 'reach at', 'mention about' — all take NO extra preposition/word.

question:
Choose the correct one-word substitution for the underlined phrase in the sentence.

Alone on the dimly lit stage, the troubled prince delivered a speech in which he voiced his innermost thoughts aloud to himself.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Soliloquy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A soliloquy is an act of speaking one's thoughts aloud when alone (or regardless of hearers), revealing the character's inner mind — exactly the underlined idea. (आत्मगत कथन)

 

• The key is that the speaker is alone and voices private thoughts to himself.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Monologue): A long speech by one person, but usually addressed to an audience or others, not private inner thought.

 

• Option 3 (Prologue): An introductory section of a play or book.

 

• Option 4 (Dialogue): A conversation between two or more people.

 

NOTE

 

• Trap: monologue vs soliloquy — a soliloquy is always the character's inner thought delivered alone; a monologue can be directed at listeners.

question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word: LACONIC
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Concise.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Laconic means using very few words; brief and to the point. (संक्षिप्त/मितभाषी)

 

• Concise — giving much information clearly and in few words — is its closest synonym.
◦ Example: His laconic reply, 'Perhaps,' revealed nothing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (Verbose): Using more words than needed — an antonym.

 

• Option 3 (Eloquent): Fluent and persuasive, not necessarily brief.

 

• Option 4 (Rambling): Lengthy and wandering — the opposite of laconic.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of laconic: terse, curt, succinct, pithy. Antonyms: verbose, garrulous, loquacious.

question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word: MITIGATE
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Aggravate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mitigate means to make something less severe, painful or serious. (कम करना/शमित करना)

 

• Aggravate — to make a problem worse — is its exact opposite.
◦ Example: Rest can mitigate the pain, while overwork will aggravate it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (Alleviate): To relieve or ease — a synonym, hence wrong for an antonym.

 

• Option 3 (Soothe): To calm or relieve — also a synonym.

 

• Option 4 (Lessen): To reduce — a synonym, not an antonym.

 

NOTE

 

• Classic antonym trap: three synonyms (alleviate, soothe, lessen) are planted as distractors — identify the odd one that reverses the meaning.

question:
Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the given idiom.

To steal someone's thunder
option_1: To criticise a person harshly in public
option_2: To create a loud and needless disturbance
option_3: To take the credit or attention for another person's idea or achievement
option_4: To frighten a rival into submission
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To take the credit or attention for another person's idea or achievement.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• To steal someone's thunder means to win praise or attention for oneself by pre-empting or using another person's idea, effort or achievement. (दूसरे का श्रेय ले लेना)

 

• ◦ Example: She announced the results first and stole her colleague's thunder.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Harsh public criticism is unrelated to the idiom.

 

• Option 2: Literal 'thunder' as noise is a trap; the idiom is figurative.

 

• Option 4: Intimidation is not the sense of the phrase.

 

NOTE

 

• The idiom comes from playwright John Dennis, whose 'thunder' stage-effect was copied by rivals. Related: 'take the wind out of one's sails'.

question:
Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the given idiom.

A storm in a teacup
option_2: A great fuss or commotion made over a trivial matter
option_3: A brief spell of unexpected calm
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. A great fuss or commotion made over a trivial matter.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A storm in a teacup describes great excitement, anger or anxiety about something that is actually very unimportant. (छोटी बात का बतंगड़)

 

• ◦ Example: Their quarrel over the seating plan was a mere storm in a teacup.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: A real calamity is the opposite — the matter here is trivial.

 

• Option 3: 'Calm' contradicts the fuss implied by 'storm'.

 

• Option 4: A hidden scheme has no connection to the idiom.

 

NOTE

 

• American variant: 'a tempest in a teapot'. Synonym idiom: 'much ado about nothing'.

question: Select the correct spelling of the word meaning 'a set of printed questions, with a choice of answers, used to gather information from people'.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Questionnaire.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct spelling is questionnaire (ques-tion-naire), meaning a printed list of questions used to collect information or opinions from people. (प्रश्नावली)
◦ Example: "Each participant was asked to fill in a detailed questionnaire about their eating habits."

 

• It comes to English from French questionnaire (from *question*); the giveaway is the double 'n' and the '-naire' ending, exactly as in *millionaire*.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (Questionaire): The commonest error — uses only a single 'n' — misspelt.

 

• Option 3 (Questionnair): Drops the final 'e' of '-naire' — misspelt.

 

• Option 4 (Questionaira): Single 'n' plus a wrong '-aira' ending — misspelt.

 

NOTE

 

• Memory hook: a questionnaire ends like millionaire ('-naire') and, like it, keeps the double 'n'. Related word: questionnaire (noun) vs the verb question.

question: Select the correct spelling of the word meaning 'diligent and taking great care to do one's work thoroughly and well'.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Conscientious.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct spelling is conscientious (con-sci-en-tious), meaning careful, diligent and guided by conscience. (कर्तव्यनिष्ठ/सतर्क)

 

• It embeds the word science/conscience: con-sci-en-tious.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (Consciencious): Uses '-cien-' twice incorrectly — misspelt.

 

• Option 3 (Conscietious): Omits the 'n' in '-ien-' — misspelt.

 

• Option 4 (Concientious): Drops the 's' after 'con' — misspelt.

 

NOTE

 

• Adverb: conscientiously. Do not confuse with 'conscious' (aware) or 'conscience' (moral sense).

question: Choose the correct one-word substitution for the given expression: 'A person who collects or studies coins and medals'.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Numismatist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A numismatist is a person who collects or studies coins, currency and medals. (मुद्राशास्त्री/सिक्का संग्रहकर्ता)

 

• The word comes from Latin numisma / Greek nomisma ('coin, current money'); the study itself is called numismatics.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (Philatelist): One who collects or studies postage stamps, not coins.

 

• Option 3 (Antiquarian): A collector or dealer in antiques and rare books in general, not specifically coins.

 

• Option 4 (Archivist): A person who maintains and manages archives/historical records, unrelated to coins.

 

NOTE

 

• Collector words often tested together: numismatist (coins), philatelist (stamps), deltiologist (postcards), oenophile (wine), bibliophile (books).

question:
Select the option that correctly fills in the blank.

The proposal was not only financially sound ________ also ecologically responsible.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. but.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed correlative conjunction pair is 'not only ... but also'. The blank must therefore be filled with but. (सहसंबंधी समुच्चयबोधक)

 

• Correct sentence: 'not only financially sound but also ecologically responsible.'

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (and): 'not only ... and also' is not a valid correlative pair.

 

• Option 3 (or): Pairs with 'either' (either ... or), not 'not only'.

 

• Option 4 (nor): Pairs with 'neither' (neither ... nor).

 

NOTE

 

• Learn the fixed pairs: either–or, neither–nor, not only–but also, both–and, whether–or, no sooner–than.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

The editor reviewed the draft twice (1)/ and, satisfied with its clarity (2)/ and structure, she finally (3)/ had the intern to format the references. (4)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (4).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The causative verb 'have' (in the sense of getting someone to do something) is followed by the bare infinitive, not 'to + verb'. So 'had the intern to format' is wrong; it must be 'had the intern format the references'. (प्रेरणार्थक क्रिया)

 

• Structure: have + object + base verb (have someone do something).
◦ Example: I had the mechanic check the brakes (not 'to check').

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: 'reviewed the draft twice' is grammatically correct.

 

• Option 2: 'satisfied with its clarity' is a correct participial phrase.

 

• Option 3: 'and structure, she finally' has no error.

 

NOTE

 

• Bare-infinitive causatives: make/let/have + object + base verb. Contrast 'get', which DOES take 'to' (got him to sign).

question:
Change the following sentence from active voice to passive voice.

The management should have informed the employees earlier.
option_1: The employees should have been informed earlier.
option_2: The employees should be informed earlier.
option_3: The employees should have informed earlier.
option_4: The employees had been informed earlier.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The employees should have been informed earlier.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The active verb is a modal perfect: 'should have informed'. Its passive form is modal + have been + past participle = 'should have been informed'. (कर्मवाच्य)

 

• The object 'the employees' becomes the subject; the agent 'the management' is dropped as unnecessary.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (should be informed): Loses the perfect aspect ('have') — wrong tense.

 

• Option 3 (should have informed): Still active in form — no 'been' + participle.

 

• Option 4 (had been informed): Changes the modal 'should' to past perfect — alters the meaning.

 

NOTE

 

• Passive of modal + have + V3 = modal + have been + V3 (must have done → must have been done).

question:
Select the sentence that contains a homonym of the highlighted word.

At dusk, a lone bat flitted silently above the moonlit orchard.
option_1: The weary travellers pitched their tent beside a glacial stream.
option_2: With calm focus, the young batsman raised his bat to face the fast bowler.
option_3: A gentle breeze stirred the curtains of the darkened room.
option_4: The rusted lantern cast long shadows across the empty courtyard.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. With calm focus, the young batsman raised his bat to face the fast bowler.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Homonyms are words with the same spelling and pronunciation but entirely different meanings. The highlighted 'bat' means a nocturnal flying mammal; the homonym 'bat' in Option 2 means the shaped wooden implement used to strike the ball in cricket. (समनाम/समशब्द)

 

• Both words are spelt b-a-t and pronounced identically, yet have unrelated origins and senses — the defining feature of a homonym.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (stream): Contains no form of the word 'bat' — unrelated.

 

• Option 3 (breeze): Contains no homonym of 'bat'.

 

• Option 4 (lantern): Unrelated to 'bat'.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Bat' can also mean 'to blink' (she did not bat an eyelid). Do not confuse homonyms (same spelling AND sound) with homophones (same sound, different spelling: 'flour/flower').

question:
Convert the following sentence from passive voice to active voice.

A new metro line is being constructed by the state government across the river.
option_1: The state government constructs a new metro line across the river.
option_2: The state government has constructed a new metro line across the river.
option_3: The state government was constructing a new metro line across the river.
option_4: The state government is constructing a new metro line across the river.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The state government is constructing a new metro line across the river.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The passive is in the present continuous ('is being constructed'). The active form of present continuous is is/are + verb-ing = 'is constructing'. (कर्तृवाच्य)

 

• The agent 'the state government' becomes the subject; the object 'a new metro line' returns to object position, and the tense (present continuous) is preserved.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (constructs): Simple present — changes the tense.

 

• Option 2 (has constructed): Present perfect — wrong tense.

 

• Option 3 (was constructing): Past continuous — wrong tense.

 

NOTE

 

• Keep the tense unchanged when converting voice: is being done → is doing; was being done → was doing.

question:
Choose the most appropriate option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

The panel has been discussing about the merger proposal for over three hours.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. discussing the merger proposal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The verb 'discuss' is transitive and takes a direct object without any preposition. Hence 'discuss the proposal', never 'discuss about the proposal'. (चर्चा करना)

 

• The present-perfect-continuous frame 'has been ... for over three hours' requires the -ing form: 'discussing the merger proposal'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (discussing on): 'discuss on' is incorrect — no preposition needed.

 

• Option 2 (discussed about): Both the preposition and the past tense break the sentence.

 

• Option 3 (discussing for): 'discuss for' is not idiomatic.

 

NOTE

 

• Other verbs taking NO preposition: enter, reach, marry, resemble, request, order, board, comprise, describe.

question:
Select the correct Direct Speech conversion of the given sentence.

She told me that she would finish the report the next day.
option_1: She said to me, "I will finish the report tomorrow."
option_2: She said to me, "I would finish the report the next day."
option_3: She said to me, "I will finish the report the next day."
option_4: She said to me, "I finished the report tomorrow."
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. She said to me, "I will finish the report tomorrow."

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Reversing indirect to direct: 'told me' → 'said to me', the pronoun 'she' → 'I', the back-shifted 'would' → 'will', and the time phrase 'the next day' → 'tomorrow'. (प्रत्यक्ष कथन)

 

• The reported clause is placed inside inverted commas with the original (present) tense restored.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Keeps the back-shifted 'would' and 'the next day' — not restored to direct form.

 

• Option 3: Correct 'will' but wrongly retains 'the next day' instead of 'tomorrow'.

 

• Option 4: 'I finished ... tomorrow' mixes past tense with a future adverb — ungrammatical.

 

NOTE

 

• Reverse-shift rules: would→will, had→have/has, the next day→tomorrow, that day→today, the previous day→yesterday.

question:
Select the option that correctly converts the given sentence into indirect speech.

The teacher said to the students, "You must submit your essays tomorrow."
option_1: The teacher told the students that they must submit their essays tomorrow.
option_2: The teacher told the students that they have to submit their essays the following day.
option_3: The teacher told the students that they had to submit their essays the next day.
option_4: The teacher said the students to submit their essays the next day.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The teacher told the students that they had to submit their essays the next day.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'said to' → 'told'; the pronoun 'you' → 'they'; the obligation 'must' → 'had to'; and the time word 'tomorrow' → 'the next day'. (अप्रत्यक्ष कथन)

 

• In reported speech, 'must' (obligation) is normally back-shifted to 'had to'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Retains 'must' and 'tomorrow' — no back-shift applied.

 

• Option 2: 'have to' is present tense, and 'following day' with present 'have' is inconsistent.

 

• Option 4: 'said the students to submit' is grammatically wrong (should be 'told' + reported clause).

 

NOTE

 

• Modal back-shifts: can→could, may→might, will→would, shall→should, must→had to. Note: 'said + to somebody' becomes 'told somebody'.

question:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph.

1. Only later was it mounted on axles to bear carts and chariots across great distances.

2. The wheel, first devised in ancient Mesopotamia, ranks among humanity's most transformative inventions.

3. Initially, it was used not for transport at all, but for shaping clay on a potter's wheel.

4. Today, its basic principle underlies almost everything, from turbines and gears to clockwork.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 2-3-1-4.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sentence 2 is the opening statement that names the topic ('The wheel ... ranks among humanity's most transformative inventions') and carries no back-reference. (आरंभिक वाक्य)

 

• Sentence 3 ('Initially, it was used ... for shaping clay') states the earliest use; Sentence 1 ('Only later was it mounted on axles') contrasts that early use with the later one; Sentence 4 ('Today, its basic principle underlies ...') gives the concluding, present-day point. Order: 2-3-1-4.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (2-1-3-4): Places 'Only later' (1) before 'Initially' (3), reversing the natural time sequence.

 

• Option 3 (3-2-1-4): Opens with 'Initially, it ...' (3), whose pronoun 'it' has no antecedent yet — the topic sentence 2 must come first.

 

• Option 4 (2-3-4-1): Puts the conclusion 'Today' (4) before the 'Only later' development (1), breaking the chronology.

 

NOTE

 

• Time-order anchors fix the flow: 'Initially' → 'Only later' → 'Today'. The sentence with no pronoun or back-reference ('The wheel ...') is the opener.

question:
Rearrange the following sentences in the correct order to make a logical passage.

1. However, unchecked tourism can strain fragile ecosystems and overburden local resources.

2. Tourism has emerged as a vital engine of economic growth for many developing nations.

3. Therefore, sustainable practices are essential to balance profit with preservation.

4. It generates employment, strengthens infrastructure, and earns valuable foreign exchange.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 2-4-1-3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sentence 2 introduces the theme ('Tourism has emerged as a vital engine of economic growth'). Sentence 4 ('It generates employment ...') elaborates the benefits. (आरंभ + विस्तार)

 

• Sentence 1 ('However, unchecked tourism can strain ...') introduces the contrast, and Sentence 3 ('Therefore, sustainable practices are essential') gives the conclusion. Order: 2-4-1-3.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (2-1-4-3): Puts the 'However' contrast (1) before the benefits (4) are stated — illogical.

 

• Option 2 (2-3-1-4): Places the conclusion 'Therefore' (3) before the contrast (1).

 

• Option 3 (4-2-1-3): Opens with 'It' (4), which lacks an antecedent.

 

NOTE

 

• Transition words fix the flow: 'However' signals a counter-point, 'Therefore' signals the conclusion — so the contrast must precede the conclusion.

question: Akbar built the 'Ibadat Khana' (House of Worship) at Fatehpur Sikri primarily for which of the following purposes?
option_4: Holding religious discussions and debates among scholars of different faiths
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Holding religious discussions and debates among scholars of different faiths.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ibadat Khana (इबादत खाना / House of Worship) was built by Akbar in 1575 CE at Fatehpur Sikri.
◦ It was a hall where Akbar invited theologians and scholars of various religions — Islam, Hinduism, Jainism, Zoroastrianism and Christianity — to hold debates.

 

• These discussions shaped Akbar's liberal outlook and led to his policy of Sulh-i-Kul (सुलह-ए-कुल / universal peace) and later the Din-i-Ilahi (दीन-ए-इलाही, 1582).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mansabdari (मनसबदारी) was Akbar's military-administrative ranking system — unrelated to the Ibadat Khana.

 

• Land-revenue reform (the Zabti/Dahsala system) was carried out by Raja Todar Mal.

 

NOTE

 

• Akbar abolished the jizya (जजिया / poll tax on non-Muslims) in 1564 and the pilgrimage tax; he was the third Mughal emperor and ruled from 1556 to 1605.

question: Which of the following is the largest island nation in the Indian Ocean by area?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Madagascar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Madagascar is the largest island nation in the Indian Ocean and the fourth-largest island in the world (after Greenland, New Guinea and Borneo), with an area of about 587,000 sq km.
◦ Capital: Antananarivo; currency: Malagasy ariary.

 

• It lies off the south-eastern coast of Africa, separated from the mainland by the Mozambique Channel.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sri Lanka (~65,600 sq km) is far smaller; Maldives is the smallest Asian nation by area and population; Mauritius has its capital at Port Louis.

 

NOTE

 

• Other Indian Ocean island nations: Seychelles (Victoria) and Comoros (Moroni). India's own island groups are the Andaman & Nicobar Islands (Bay of Bengal) and Lakshadweep (Arabian Sea).

question: The 'PM SVANidhi' scheme of the Government of India is primarily aimed at providing which of the following?
option_1: Affordable micro-credit (working-capital loans) to urban street vendors
option_2: Free LPG connections to rural households
option_3: Piped water supply to every rural household
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Affordable micro-credit (working-capital loans) to urban street vendors.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• PM SVANidhi (PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi / पीएम स्वनिधि) was launched in June 2020 by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
◦ It provides collateral-free working-capital loans (in tranches of ₹10,000, ₹20,000 and ₹50,000) to urban street vendors.

 

• It promotes digital transactions through cashback incentives.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Free LPG → PM Ujjwala Yojana.
◦ Piped water to rural households → Jal Jeevan Mission.
◦ Crop insurance → PM Fasal Bima Yojana.

 

NOTE

 

• Key urban-infrastructure schemes: AMRUT (water supply & sewerage), Smart Cities Mission, PMAY-Urban (housing) and Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban.

question: Which style of Indian temple architecture is characterised by a pyramidal tower called the 'Vimana' and a gateway tower known as the 'Gopuram'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Dravida style.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Dravida (द्रविड़) style developed in South India and is marked by:
◦ A stepped, pyramidal tower over the sanctum called the Vimana (विमान).
◦ Tall gateway towers in the enclosure walls called Gopuram (गोपुरम).

 

• Classic example: the Brihadeeswarar Temple, Thanjavur, built by Rajaraja Chola I.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nagara style (North India) has a curvilinear tower called Shikhara (शिखर) and no boundary gateways.
◦ Vesara style is a hybrid of Nagara and Dravida (Chalukyas, Hoysalas of the Deccan).
◦ Kalinga style (Odisha) is a regional sub-type of Nagara — e.g. Konark and Lingaraja temples.

 

NOTE

 

• Parts of a temple: Garbhagriha (sanctum), Mandapa (hall), Antarala (vestibule) and Amalaka & Kalasha (crowning elements of a Nagara shikhara).

question: The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, which came into force on 1 July 2024, replaced which of the following colonial-era laws?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Three new criminal laws came into force on 1 July 2024:
◦ Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 replaced the Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860.
◦ Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973.
◦ Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023 replaced the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.

 

• The BNSS governs criminal procedure — arrest, investigation, trial and bail — and introduced Zero FIR, e-FIR and time-bound investigation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The BNS has 358 sections (the IPC had 511); the BNSS has 531 sections. The laws were piloted by the Ministry of Home Affairs under Home Minister Amit Shah.

 

NOTE

 

• A Zero FIR can be registered at any police station regardless of jurisdiction. The Indian Contract Act, 1872 is a civil law and was not replaced by these criminal codes.

question: 'Sudarshan Setu', inaugurated in February 2024 and recognised as India's longest cable-stayed bridge, is located in which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Gujarat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sudarshan Setu (सुदर्शन सेतु) was inaugurated by PM Narendra Modi on 25 February 2024.
◦ It is India's longest cable-stayed bridge (~2.32 km) and connects Okha on the mainland with Beyt Dwarka island in Gujarat.

 

• It was earlier known as the Signature Bridge.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Atal Setu (MTHL), India's longest sea bridge (~21.8 km), opened in January 2024 in Mumbai, Maharashtra.
◦ The Bhupen Hazarika Setu (Dhola–Sadiya) in Assam is India's longest river bridge.

 

NOTE

 

• Beyt Dwarka is associated with Lord Krishna; Dwarka is one of the four Char Dham pilgrimage sites of India.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Sardar Sarovar Dam and choose the CORRECT option:

1. It is built on the Narmada River.

2. It is located in the state of Gujarat.

3. It is the tallest dam in India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sardar Sarovar Dam (सरदार सरोवर बांध) is built on the Narmada River near Kevadia (Ekta Nagar) in Gujarat — so Statements 1 and 2 are correct.
◦ It is the centrepiece of the Narmada Valley Project and benefits Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Rajasthan.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect — India's tallest dam is the Tehri Dam on the Bhagirathi river in Uttarakhand (~260.5 m); the Sardar Sarovar is the second tallest concrete dam.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Statue of Unity (of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel), the world's tallest statue, stands near this dam.
◦ The Narmada Bachao Andolan, led by Medha Patkar, opposed raising the dam's height.

 

NOTE

 

• The Narmada flows westward into the Arabian Sea through a rift valley. Other major dams: Hirakud (Mahanadi), Bhakra Nangal (Sutlej) and Nagarjuna Sagar (Krishna).

question: According to Koppen's climate classification, the 'Aw' (tropical savanna) type of climate is found largely over which of the following regions of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Most of the peninsular plateau.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Koppen's classification, 'Aw' denotes a tropical savanna (wet-and-dry) climate with a dry winter.
◦ In India it prevails over most of the peninsular plateau south of the Tropic of Cancer.

 

• Here 'A' = tropical (mean temperature of the coldest month above 18°C) and 'w' = dry winter.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• 'Amw' = tropical monsoon → western coast (including Kerala) and the Western Ghats.
◦ 'BWhw' = hot desert → Thar / western Rajasthan.
◦ 'Cwg' = humid subtropical with dry winter → north Indian (Ganga) plains.
◦ 'E' = polar/tundra → the Himalayas.

 

NOTE

 

• Koppen used the capital letters A, B, C, D and E for the five major climatic groups; his scheme is based on mean temperature and precipitation with vegetation as an index.

question: The vibrant folk dance 'Lavani', traditionally performed to the beats of the 'Dholki' drum, is most closely associated with which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Maharashtra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lavani (लावणी) is a popular folk dance and song form of Maharashtra, usually performed by women in a nine-yard saree to the rhythm of the Dholki (ढोलकी) drum.
◦ The word derives from *lavanya* meaning 'beauty', and it is often presented in the Tamasha folk-theatre tradition.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Folk dances of nearby states:
◦ Garba & Dandiya-Raas — Gujarat.
◦ Dekhni & Fugdi — Goa.
◦ Yakshagana & Dollu Kunitha — Karnataka.

 

NOTE

 

• Other folk dances of Maharashtra include Tamasha, Koli (fishermen's dance) and Lezim. India's eight classical dances are Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Mohiniyattam, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Sattriya and Manipuri.

question: Which of the following Harappan sites is well known for the discovery of a large dockyard, indicating it was an important centre of maritime trade?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Lothal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lothal (लोथल), in Gujarat near the Gulf of Khambhat, is famous for its artificial dockyard — evidence of a flourishing maritime and bead trade.
◦ It was excavated by S. R. Rao.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kalibangan (Rajasthan) — ploughed field and fire altars.
◦ Dholavira (Gujarat) — water reservoirs and a signboard; a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
◦ Rakhigarhi (Haryana) — the largest Harappan site in India.
◦ Harappa — granaries; Mohenjodaro — the Great Bath.

 

NOTE

 

• The Indus Valley Civilisation (~2500–1900 BCE) was first discovered in 1921 at Harappa by Dayaram Sahni; Mohenjodaro was excavated by R. D. Banerji in 1922.

question: In the sport of Kabaddi, how many players from each team are present on the court at the start of a match?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 7.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Kabaddi (कबड्डी), each team fields seven (7) players on the court, along with up to five substitutes.
◦ A raider enters the opponent's half chanting 'kabaddi' to tag defenders and return without being tackled.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Players on field by sport: Cricket 11, Hockey 11, Football 11, Kabaddi 7, Water Polo 7, Volleyball 6, Basketball 5, Kho-Kho 9.

 

NOTE

 

• Kabaddi is the state game of Tamil Nadu; India has dominated the Kabaddi World Cup. It featured as a full medal sport at the 1990 Beijing Asian Games, and the Pro Kabaddi League began in 2014.

question: The system of 'Dyarchy' (dual government) was first introduced in the provinces of British India by which of the following Acts?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Government of India Act, 1919.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Government of India Act, 1919 (the Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms) introduced Dyarchy (द्वैध शासन) in the provinces.
◦ Provincial subjects were divided into 'Reserved' (administered by the Governor and his council) and 'Transferred' (administered by ministers responsible to the legislature).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Government of India Act, 1935 abolished provincial dyarchy and introduced provincial autonomy, while proposing dyarchy at the Centre (which was never implemented).
◦ The Indian Councils Act, 1861 restored legislative powers to the Bombay and Madras presidencies.

 

NOTE

 

• The 1919 Act also created a bicameral central legislature. It was named after Secretary of State Edwin Montagu and Viceroy Lord Chelmsford.

question:
Consider the following statements about India's performance at the 2024 Paris Olympics and choose the CORRECT option:

1. Neeraj Chopra won a silver medal in the men's javelin throw.

2. Manu Bhaker became the first Indian to win two medals at a single Olympic Games since independence.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Both 1 and 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the 2024 Paris Olympics, India won a total of 6 medals (1 silver and 5 bronze).
◦ Neeraj Chopra won silver in the men's javelin throw (gold went to Pakistan's Arshad Nadeem) — Statement 1 is correct.
◦ Manu Bhaker won two bronze medals (women's 10 m air pistol and the mixed-team 10 m air pistol), becoming the first Indian to win two medals at a single Olympics since independence — Statement 2 is correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indian men's hockey team won bronze; wrestler Aman Sehrawat won bronze and became India's youngest individual Olympic medallist.

 

NOTE

 

• Neeraj Chopra had won gold at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics. Paris 2024 was the 33rd Summer Olympics; the 2028 Games will be held in Los Angeles.

question: The book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India', which developed the 'Drain of Wealth' theory, was written by whom?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Dadabhai Naoroji.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901) was written by Dadabhai Naoroji (दादाभाई नौरोजी), known as the 'Grand Old Man of India'.
◦ In it he systematically developed the 'Drain of Wealth' theory — that British rule was draining India's wealth to England.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Naoroji was the first Indian to be elected to the British House of Commons and served thrice as President of the Indian National Congress.

 

NOTE

 

• Other freedom-era works: 'Gita Rahasya' – Bal Gangadhar Tilak; 'Unhappy India' – Lala Lajpat Rai; 'Hind Swaraj' – M. K. Gandhi; 'India for Indians' – C. R. Das.

question:
Consider the following statements about the ICC Champions Trophy 2025 and choose the CORRECT option:

1. India defeated New Zealand in the final to win the title.

2. The final was played at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Both 1 and 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the final of the ICC Champions Trophy 2025, played on 9 March 2025, India defeated New Zealand by 4 wickets — Statement 1 is correct.
◦ The final was held at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium, as India played all its matches in Dubai on a hybrid-hosting model (Pakistan being the official host) — Statement 2 is correct.

 

• This was India's third Champions Trophy title (2002 shared with Sri Lanka, 2013, and 2025).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rohit Sharma captained India; Rachin Ravindra was Player of the Match in the final, while Kuldeep Yadav and India's spinners were pivotal. Varun Chakravarthy starred with the ball in the tournament.

 

NOTE

 

• The Champions Trophy 2025 was hosted by Pakistan (its first ICC event since 1996), with India's fixtures moved to the UAE. The tournament was earlier known as the ICC Knockout Trophy.

question: The collective responsibility of the Union Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha is enshrined in which Article of the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Article 75.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 75(3) provides that the Union Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (लोक सभा).
◦ Thus, if the Lok Sabha passes a no-confidence motion, the entire Council of Ministers must resign.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 74 — Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President.
◦ Article 78 — duties of the Prime Minister to furnish information to the President.
◦ Article 164 — collective responsibility of the State Council of Ministers to the Legislative Assembly.

 

NOTE

 

• Collective responsibility is a feature of the parliamentary system, borrowed from the British Constitution. Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President (Article 75(2)).

question:
Read the following statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R) and choose the correct option:

Assertion (A): Chandrayaan-3 made India the first country to land a spacecraft near the south pole of the Moon.

Reason (R): The mission's lander was named 'Vikram' and its rover was named 'Pragyan'.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chandrayaan-3 soft-landed on 23 August 2023, making India the first country to land near the lunar south pole and the fourth to achieve a soft landing on the Moon (after the USSR, USA and China) — A is TRUE.
◦ Its lander was named 'Vikram' (after Vikram Sarabhai) and its rover 'Pragyan' — R is TRUE.

 

• However, the naming of the lander and rover has nothing to do with why India was first to the south pole — so R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• It was launched by an LVM-3 rocket from Sriharikota. 23 August is now observed as National Space Day, and the landing site was named 'Shiv Shakti Point'.

 

NOTE

 

• ISRO was founded in 1969; its first chairman was Vikram Sarabhai. India's first satellite was Aryabhata (1975).

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to impose 'President's Rule' in a state on the ground of failure of constitutional machinery?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Article 356.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 356 allows the President to impose President's Rule (राष्ट्रपति शासन) in a state when its government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution — a failure of constitutional machinery.
◦ It is usually invoked on a report of the Governor of the state.

 

• A proclamation under Article 356 must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within two months and can normally continue for a maximum of three years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 352 — National Emergency (war, external aggression or armed rebellion).
◦ Article 360 — Financial Emergency.
◦ Article 371 — special provisions for certain states like Maharashtra, Gujarat and Nagaland.

 

NOTE

 

• In the S. R. Bommai case (1994), the Supreme Court ruled that the imposition of President's Rule is subject to judicial review. Article 356 is also called 'State Emergency' and falls under Part XVIII of the Constitution.

question: The process in which two lighter atomic nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus, releasing an enormous amount of energy, is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Nuclear fusion.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nuclear fusion (नाभिकीय संलयन) is the combining of two light nuclei (such as hydrogen isotopes) into a heavier nucleus, releasing huge energy.
◦ It is the source of the energy of the Sun and other stars (hydrogen fusing into helium).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nuclear fission is the splitting of a heavy nucleus (e.g. Uranium-235) into lighter nuclei — used in atom bombs and nuclear reactors.
◦ Fusion requires extremely high temperature and pressure; the hydrogen bomb is based on fusion.

 

NOTE

 

• In both fission and fusion a small mass defect is converted into energy according to Einstein's equation E = mc². Fusion releases more energy per unit mass than fission.

question: The 'Sekrenyi' festival, celebrated as a festival of purification, is associated with which tribe of Nagaland?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Angami.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sekrenyi (सेक्रेन्यी) is a festival of purification and sanctification celebrated by the Angami tribe of Nagaland, usually in February.
◦ It is also called Phousanyi, during which the menfolk undergo ritual purification.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Naga tribes and their festivals: Ao — Moatsu and Tsungremong; Konyak — Aoleang; Sema (Sumi) — Tuluni; Chakhesang — Sukrunye.

 

NOTE

 

• The Hornbill Festival, the 'Festival of Festivals', is held every December at Kisama near Kohima and showcases all Naga tribes. Nagaland attained statehood in 1963.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding currency convertibility in India and choose the correct option:

Statement 1: The Indian rupee is fully convertible on the current account.

Statement 2: The Indian rupee is fully convertible on the capital account.
option_3: Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct
option_4: Neither Statement 1 nor Statement 2 is correct
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Only Statement 1 is correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India adopted full current account convertibility in 1994 (under Article VIII of the IMF), so the rupee is freely convertible for trade in goods and services, remittances, etc. — Statement 1 is correct.
◦ On the capital account the rupee is only partially convertible; capital flows are regulated by the RBI under FEMA — Statement 2 is incorrect.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The current account covers trade, services, income and transfers; the capital account covers investments, loans and banking capital.
◦ The Tarapore Committee examined the road-map for full capital account convertibility.

 

NOTE

 

• FEMA (1999) replaced FERA (1973). Convertibility means the freedom to convert domestic currency into foreign currency and vice versa at market-determined exchange rates.

question:
Read the following statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R) and choose the correct option:

Assertion (A): The World Bank launched the 'Business Ready' (B-READY) report as a new assessment of the business and investment climate.

Reason (R): The earlier 'Ease of Doing Business' report was discontinued following allegations of data irregularities.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The World Bank discontinued its 'Ease of Doing Business' report in 2021 after an internal review found data irregularities/manipulation — R is TRUE.
◦ As its successor, the World Bank released the first 'Business Ready' (B-READY) report in October 2024 — A is TRUE.

 

• B-READY was created specifically to replace the discontinued Doing Business report, so R correctly explains A.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• B-READY assesses the business environment across pillars such as the regulatory framework, public services and operational efficiency for a large set of economies.

 

NOTE

 

• The World Bank (HQ: Washington D.C.) and the IMF were established at the Bretton Woods Conference, 1944. Other indices: the Global Hunger Index and the Human Development Index (UNDP).

question: The Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices (MRTP) Act was enacted in 1969 with the primary objective of:
option_3: Providing an employment guarantee in rural areas
option_4: Preventing the concentration of economic power and monopolies
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Preventing the concentration of economic power and monopolies.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The MRTP Act, 1969 (एकाधिकार एवं प्रतिबंधात्मक व्यापार व्यवहार अधिनियम) aimed to prevent the concentration of economic power in a few hands and to control monopolies and restrictive trade practices.
◦ It drew on the recommendations of the Monopolies Inquiry Commission and the Hazari Committee.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Under the License Raj, industrial licensing often allowed large houses to block competitors; the 1991 New Economic Policy (LPG reforms) dismantled most industrial licensing.
◦ The MRTP Act was replaced by the Competition Act, 2002, which set up the Competition Commission of India (CCI).

 

NOTE

 

• The 1991 reforms — Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation — were introduced by Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh under PM P. V. Narasimha Rao.

question:
Consider the following statements about 'Project Cheetah' in India and choose the CORRECT option:

1. The cheetahs were reintroduced at Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh.

2. It is the world's first inter-continental translocation of a large wild carnivore.

3. The first batch of cheetahs was brought from Australia.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Project Cheetah was launched on 17 September 2022, when cheetahs were released at Kuno National Park, Madhya Pradesh — Statement 1 is correct.
◦ It is the world's first inter-continental translocation of a large wild carnivore — Statement 2 is correct.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect — the first batch of 8 cheetahs came from Namibia (September 2022), followed by 12 from South Africa (February 2023). Australia has no wild cheetahs.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The cheetah was declared extinct in India in 1952; the African cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus) was reintroduced. Kuno lies in the Sheopur district of Madhya Pradesh.

 

NOTE

 

• India launched Project Tiger in 1973 and Project Elephant in 1992. Other MP tiger reserves include Kanha, Bandhavgarh, Pench and Panna.

question: In India, the nodal department responsible for managing the Government's disinvestment and privatisation of Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) is the:
option_2: Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM)
option_3: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• DIPAM (निवेश एवं लोक परिसंपत्ति प्रबंधन विभाग), under the Ministry of Finance, manages the government's disinvestment of its equity in PSUs.
◦ It was earlier the Department of Disinvestment, renamed DIPAM in 2016.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Disinvestment is the sale of the government's equity stake in a PSU; in strategic disinvestment, majority stake and management control are transferred to a private entity — e.g. Air India to the Tata Group (2022).

 

NOTE

 

• NITI Aayog identifies PSUs for strategic disinvestment; SEBI regulates the securities market; the RBI is the central bank. CPSEs are graded as Maharatna, Navratna and Miniratna.
